subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for 70B model — KV cache & quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sarah Huang <sarah@lumenhealth.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing request — 70B model, long context

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the earlier call. To summarize our requirements so your team can size Dedicated capacity:
- Model: internally forked 70B (same architecture as xL-70)
- Typical context: customers will append up to ~128k tokens of history for retrieval-augmented generation; average context ~80k tokens
- Generation: average output 1.5k tokens, spikes to 4k tokens
- Latency SLO: 1st-token P50 ~250-400ms, P95 under 1.2s
- Concurrency: steady 10 concurrent requests, peak 25 concurrent (5–10 min bursts)
- Availability: 99.9% target, regional (US-East) deployment
- Security: SOC2 + perimeter controls (we can provide questionnaire)

One important question: we expect to use quantization to reduce costs. We are comfortable with 8-bit/4-bit weight quantization for the model weights so long as quality delta is <2% on our eval sets. We understand KV cache usually remains higher precision; we want tradeoffs and a recommended Dedicated configuration.

Can you put together a recommended hardware footprint (GPU types and counts per replica), implications of int8 vs int4 quantization, KV cache memory estimates, and a ballpark monthly committed price for Dedicated capacity?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow if useful.

—Sarah
Sarah Huang
Head of AI Platforms
Lumen Health

Sarah — thanks, this is great detail. We can definitely size this. Quick clarifying Qs before we do detailed math:
1) For the 128k context case, is that "active" context that must be resident in KV cache for the entire conversation, or can you partition/evict older segments?
2) Do you have a policy for prefix caching vs full-session KV retention?
3) Any hard constraint on single-request latency during peak bursts vs average loads?

I'll pull together an internal calc and a recommended config with two scenarios: (A) int8 quantized weights (safer, broadly supported) and (B) aggressive int4 (higher risk but cost-lower). Note: KV cache size typically dominates GPU memory for very long contexts because it remains higher precision; quantizing weights reduces model footprint but doesn't proportionally shrink KV.

I'll aim to send a recommended footprint + ballpark committed pricing and an attachment with the calc by end of day tomorrow.

Cheers,
Diego

Diego —
1) Active KV: we need the last 128k tokens to be addressable at inference time for full-session RAG. We can tolerate some eviction for older sessions (LRU after 24h).
2) We do plan to use prefix caching for common system prompts, but user histories are required live.
3) Latency during 25-concurrency bursts: if P95 slips slightly above 1.2s for a short period we're OK, but consistent degradation is unacceptable.

Thanks — Sarah
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Lumen Health — initial sizing thoughts (rough numbers)

Team — pulling together rough numbers for Lumen Health (70B, 128k active KV). High-level assumptions: model architecture similar to 70B public families; baseline fp16 weight footprint ~140GB; int8 ~70GB; int4 ~35GB (order-of-magnitude). KV cache: because KV stores per-token key+value in higher precision, it is the main driver for long-context. For our calc I used a conservative per-token KV footprint of ~1.6KB (keys+values across all heads in fp16). That yields: 
- 128k tokens * 1.6KB ≈ 200MB (per session) — note: per-session cache stored across shards; aggregate active KV memory depends on concurrent sessions.

Concurrency math (steady / peak):
- Steady 10 concurrent sessions with full 128k active KV: ~10 * 200MB = 2GB KV active RAM across the cluster (sharded across GPUs).
- Peak 25 concurrent: ~25 * 200MB = 5GB active KV.

Model weights + KV per replica (rough):
- int8 weights (70GB) + reserved GPU working memory (12–18GB) + per-gpu slice of KV (depends on sharding) → realistically we can fit a single replica on 2 x H100-80GB with model-parallel=2 and TPU-style ops; 1 x H100 is tight unless we use aggressive operator fusion + int4.
- int4 path: weights ~35GB, but we still need working memory + KV per GPU; possible on 1 x H100 with 80GB if we also limit batch size and accept longer tail latency.

Recommendation (tradeoff oriented):
- Conservative, latency-safe: 2x H100-80GB per replica, replicate N=2 for HA and throughput. This supports spikes, keeps P95 headroom, and simplifies rollouts.
- Cost-optimized: int8 + sharding on 2x A100-80GB (if customer prefers A100 availability) or 1x H100 + NVMe-backed offload for weights + careful batching — lower capex but more brittle on latency.

Operational notes:
- KV remains fp16/bf16; quantization of weights does not meaningfully shrink KV. So focusing on smarter KV management (prefix caches, LRU eviction, hot-session pinning) buys more GPU savings than weight-only quantization.
- We should instrument token-level tracing and a per-session KV memory dashboard during the pilot to validate assumptions.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with the per-token assumptions and a few GPU mix options. Priya/Rishi: please sanity-check the model-parallel numbers and the per-GPU working-memory safety buffer I used (12–18GB).

Thanks — Diego
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Lumen Health — initial sizing thoughts (rough numbers)

Quick sanity check notes:
- Per-token KV estimate: 1.6KB is conservative but fine for planning. For some 70B variants that use more keys/values the per-token could approach ~2.2KB; I'll add that scenario to the sheet.
- Model memory: 140GB fp16 is a good upper bound. With int8 we should plan for ~75–80GB after allocator/fragmentation overhead. So 2 x 80GB GPUs gives headroom.
- Replication: For 99.9% availability and the burst profile, recommend 2 replicas (active/standby) each scaled to handle peak concurrency (25). If they want aggressive cost-savings, we can present a single-replica cost with auto-fallback to a hosted compatible model during sustained overloads.
- Networking: NVLink for intra-host sharding is strongly preferred to minimize cross-host latency for KV fetches. That rules out cheap cloud instances without adequate GPU interconnect.

I'll update the spreadsheet with 3 scenarios: (A) latency-safe: 2x H100 per replica, 2 replicas; (B) cost-tuned: int8 on 2x A100 per replica, 2 replicas + aggressive prefix caching; (C) experimental: int4 single H100 + strict throttling (pilot only).

Priya

Sarah / procurement team —

Thanks again for the clarity. Attached are: (1) rdw_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx with per-token/KV assumptions and three hardware scenarios, (2) kv_cache_estimates.csv with a per-session breakdown, and (3) a draft Dedicated quote. High-level recommendation below.

Summary recommendation (production-ready, recommended):
- Config: 2 x H100-80GB GPUs per replica (tensor parallel 2) with 2 replicas (active/standby) in US-East.
- Why: int8 quantization reduces weight footprint but KV cache (fp16) drives memory. Two H100s per replica gives consistent headroom for concurrency spikes and keeps P95 latency within your target. NVLink intra-host recommended.
- Expected monthly committed price (ballpark): $60k–$90k / month for the dedicated cluster described (includes support and 24/7 monitoring). Final price depends on contract term and commitment level.

Cost-optimized alternative (if Lumen wants lower commitment):
- Config: int8 weights on 2 x A100-80GB per replica, 2 replicas + aggressive prefix caching and workload shaping. Price estimate: $40k–$60k / month.

Pilot approach:
1) 30-day pilot on the cost-optimized config (A100s) with staged traffic mirroring + instrumentation for KV utilization.
2) If pilot confirms latency & quality, transition to production config (H100s) with a 30-day warm-up and canary.

Requested next steps:
- Please confirm whether Lumen wants us to price the latency-safe H100 config or start with the cost-optimized pilot.
- If proceeding, procurement can send a PO referencing RDW-DEAL-2026-1184. I'll loop in Solutions Engineering for a kickoff.

Attachments: rdw_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx (workbook), kv_cache_estimates.csv (per-session math), 70b-dedicated-quote-draft.pdf (draft pricing).

If you want a live run-through of the spreadsheet I can schedule a 30-min session tomorrow.
